nodes.name: Acid treatment of NF
nodes.procedure: The electrodes were ultrasonicated for 15 min in 2 M HCl and sprayed with 1 M HNO₃ and left to react for 1 hour. After treatment, they were thoroughly rinsed with deionized (DI) water and ethanol, then dried in air.
nodes.source_text: For the acid-treated NF (NF_acid) sample, the electrodes were ultrasonicated for 15 min in 2 M HCl and sprayed with 1 M HNO₃ and left to react for 1 hour.

nodes.name: Fe spraying on acid-treated NF
nodes.procedure: The NF_acid electrode underwent the 2 M HCl acid treatment followed by spraying with 1 M Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O and a 10-minute reaction time. The electrode was then rinsed with DI water and ethanol, and dried in air.
nodes.source_text: The Fe-sprayed NF (NF_Fe) electrode underwent the 2 M HCl acid treatment... followed by spraying with 1 M Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O and a 10-minute reaction time.

nodes.name: Ni(111) cleaning cycles
nodes.procedure: The Ni(111) single crystal underwent a rigorous cleaning procedure in an UHV chamber with a base pressure of 1×10⁻¹⁰ mbar. The cleaning process involved multiple cycles of 3 kV Ar⁺ ion sputtering for 10 minutes, followed by annealing at 800 K in an oxygen atmosphere (5×10⁻⁸ mbar) to remove carbon contaminants and subsequently in a hydrogen atmosphere (5×10⁻⁸ mbar) to reduce oxide species. The sample was then subjected to additional sputtering and annealing cycles under UHV conditions using the same parameters. The cleanliness of the surface was verified with STM.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF₀ shows smooth, flat surface regions consistent with large crystalline Ni grains; NF_acid displays visibly roughened surface morphology; NF_Fe exhibits pronounced cavities with precipitated Fe-phase particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) imaging (Fig. 1a) reveals that each fiber of the NF₀ shows smooth, flat surface regions consistent with large crystalline Ni grains, whereas the NF_acid displays a visibly roughened surface morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals substantial reduction in NiO content for both NF_acid and NF_Fe electrodes, consistent with acid treatment effects on native surface oxide layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis reveals a substantial reduction in NiO content for both NF_acid and NF_Fe electrodes, consistent with the expected effects of acid treatment on native surface oxide layers (Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) estimated from j-ν relationship in non-faradaic region using allometric model: NF₀ = 45.9 ± 5.1 μF cm⁻², NF_acid = 72.4 ± 0.5 μF cm⁻², NF_Fe = 93.9 ± 0.5 μF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results showed the expected increase in double-layer capacitance (C_dl) from 45.9 ± 5.1 μF cm⁻² for the NF₀ to 72.4 ± 0.5 μF cm⁻² for the NF_acid (Fig. S4), based on anodic currents. This value further increased to 93.9 ± 0.5 μF cm⁻² for the NF_Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(111)_flat exhibits 10-50 nm wide terraces with few steps; Ni(111)_step shows hillock-like features with 10.7 ± 3.3 nm base size, 1.1 ± 0.4 nm height (5 steps); Fe preferentially deposits at step edges on both flat and stepped surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni(111)_flat exhibited extended 10-50 nm wide terraces, separated by a few regular single atomic steps ... The hillocks had an average bottom lateral size of 10.7 ± 3.3 nm narrowing from base to apex and an average height of 1.1 ± 0.4 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s after H₂O droplet exposure: O²⁻ at 529.8 eV, OH⁻ at 531.4 eV across all samples; post-500 K UHV heating retention: Ni(111)_flat 7%, Ni(111)_step 42%, Fe/Ni(111)_flat 31%, Fe/Ni(111)_step 95%; post-heating O²⁻/OH⁻ ratios: 1.40 (Ni flat), 1.07 (Ni step), 2.64 (Fe flat), 0.92 (Fe step).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni(111)_flat showed almost complete reduction with a 93% reduction in total O 1s signal ... In contrast, Ni(111)_step retained 42%, showing a distinct difference in the oxide layer. Fe-deposited samples showed even greater retention of O species: Fe/Ni(111)_step retained 95%, Fe/Ni(111)_flat only 31%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-heated Ni(111)_flat shows NiO(100) islands (~1.3 ML, 4.2 Å spacing) on terraces with minor Ni(OH)₂; confirms spatial separation of oxide (terraces) and hydroxide phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STM image of the post-heated Ni(111)_flat sample showed surface island growth ... revealed a square atomic lattice with ∼4.2 Å spacing, consistent with the NiO(100) phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Ni 2p: Ni(111)_step enriched in NiOOH vs NiO compared to flat (OH⁻/O²⁻ ratios 9.1 vs 4.2); Fe/Ni(111)_step shows higher NiOOH/NiO ratio (0.68) than Fe/Ni(111)_flat (0.48).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p data, both Ni(111)_flat and Ni(111)_step exhibited dominant NiO and NiOOH components ... where the OH⁻/O²⁻ ratios were found to be 4.2 for Ni(111)_flat and 9.1 for Ni(111)_step.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p₃/₂ post-H₂O droplet and annealing: Fe/Ni(111)_flat mainly Fe²⁺ (FeO/FeOOH ratio 5.2), Fe/Ni(111)_step favors Fe³⁺ (FeO/FeOOH ratio 0.8); post-OER both show predominantly FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Using procedures developed for fitting ... point to Fe/Ni(111)_flat that consisted mainly of Fe²⁺ (FeO/FeOOH ratio 5.2), while Fe/Ni(111)_step favored a higher amount of Fe³⁺ (FeO/FeOOH ratio 0.8).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-heated Ni(111)_step shows clusters averaging 14.0 ± 2.3 nm lateral size and 1.0 ± 0.3 nm height, indicating cluster growth relative to pristine state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: On the stepped surface, STM offered limited information due to roughness ... Ni(111)_step displayed clusters averaging 14.0 ± 2.3 nm lateral size and 1.0 ± 0.3 nm height (Fig. S12), indicating cluster growth relative to the pristine state.
